blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We introduce the word thermalization hypothesis according to which in a literary work there are effective interactions between words that drive them to thermalization where their word frequency distribution is the same as for the phenomenon of Rayleigh-Jeans (RJ) thermalization and condensation. In this concept, the different words play a role of classical oscillators (particles) and their word frequencies, or related tokens, are analogous to certain filling factors over energy state levels. The thermalization process is characterized by the conservation of total system energy, or total number of words/tokens, and total probability norm, or total number of different words. We apply this approach to analyze 16 literary works, including Bible, complete works of Shakespeare, and data from American National Corpus. We show that for these cases the effective system energy is very low and thus there is the RJ condensation phenomenon with a big fraction of total probability concentrated at the lowest energy states corresponding to a big fraction of rare words appearing only once or twice in the whole text. Such a RJ condensation is observed for light propagation in multimode optical fibers and other physical systems. We relate the thermalization of words to the recently proposed wealth thermalization for households in world countries. The economy concepts of Lorenz and Pareto curves, and also Zipf curves, are applied to the word frequency distributions of the selected 16 cases and it is shown that the thermalization theory gives a strikingly good description of real data.
blocks.zh: 我们提出"热化假说",根据这个假说,在文学作品中,词之间的有效相互作用促使它们实现热化,其词频分布与Rayleigh-Jeans(RJ)热化和收缩现象相同. 在这个概念中,不同的单词扮演了古典振荡器(粒子)的角色,而它们的单词频率,或相關的符號等都与某些填充因素相类似而高于能态水平. 热化过程的特点是保存系统能量总量,或单词/托词总量,和总概率规范,或不同单词总量. 我们采用这种方法来分析16部文学作品,包括"圣经",莎士比亚的完整作品,以及美国国家公司的数据. 我们显示,对于这些案例来说,有效的系统能量非常低,因此存在RJ收缩现象,总概率的一大部分集中在最低的能态上,相当于稀有词的一大分量只出现在了整个文本中一到两次. 这种RJ收缩在多模光纤和其他物理系统中用于光传播。 我们把文字的热化与最近提出的世界各国家庭的财富热化联系起来。 Lorenz和Pareto曲线的经济概念,以及Zipf曲线,被应用到所选取的16个案例的单词频率分布上,并且显示热化理论对真实数据给出了显著良好的描述.

blocks.en:
To understand the properties of the whole
word frequency distribution
in literary works, we introduce
the WOrd Thermalization Hypothesis (WOTH)
according to which the semantic laws, meanings and
literary work concepts create links and interactions
between words that drive the word frequency
distribution to thermalization of
words. These links and interactions
between words describe the classical objects
and thus the physical laws of classical mechanics Landau and Lifshitz (1976) ; Zakharov, L’vov, and Falkovich (1992) conduct the whole system to a
stationary thermal word frequency distribution.
According to the laws of statistical physics this
distribution is given by the Rayleigh-Jeans (RJ) thermalization and
condensation phenomenon well studied in various physical systems.
In physics the RJ distribution describes usually classical
particles or objects where the thermalization appears due to
nonlinear interactions between particles or due to
a system contact with an external thermal bath
(see e.g. Frahm and Shepelyansky (2023) ; Ermann, Chepelianskii, and Shepelyansky (2026) ).
In this context, it is also assumed that the system
evolution conserves two quantities (integrals of motion)
being the system energy and the probability
norm (or number of particles).

In physical systems, RJ thermalization and condensation
were found in numerical simulations and experiments
with light propagation in multimode
optical fibers Connaughton et al. (2005) ; Krupa et al. (2016) ; Baudin et al. (2020) ; Ermann, Chepelianskii, and Shepelyansky (2026) .
The surprising feature of the RJ thermal distribution
is that at low total system energy
a large probability fraction (or number of particles)
is concentrated at low energy states
and only a very small fraction is located at high energy states.
In fact the RJ condensation belongs to
a more generic phenomenon of statistical mechanics known as the
constraint-driven condensation Evans et al. (2010) ; Szavits-Nossan, Evans, and Majumdar (2014) ; Filiasi et al. (2014) that describes
such diverse physical systems as jamming in traffic,
coalescence in granular media,
gelation in networks Szavits-Nossan, Evans, and Majumdar (2014) and financial data analysis Filiasi et al. (2014) .

The striking feature for the wealth distribution in world countries
is the strong inequality of wealth of households
as demonstrated e.g. in Piketty (2014) ; Chancel et al. (2022) ; Roach et al. (2003) .
Thus, according to Chancel et al. (2022) for the whole world
50% of the population owns only 2% of total wealth, while the top 10%
owns 75% of total wealth, of which 38% is held by the top 1% alone.
The emergence of the phase of very poor households
and the oligarchic phase of very rich ones
is naturally explained in the framework of the RJ thermalization approach.
In this context, the wealth of a household is analogous to an energy level of a
physical system.

fraction w w of total wealth as a function of the cumulated fraction

The line w = h w=h corresponds to the case of perfect
equipartition. It is useful to define the Gini coefficient G ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] G\in[0,1] ,
being the doubled area between the equipartition line and the
Lorenz curve. Thus the Gini coefficient characterizes the global inequality of the wealth
distribution, i.e. large of values of G G close
to unity correspond to a strong inequality.

blocks.en:
In this work, we presented the concept
of RJ thermalization and condensation
of words in literary works (or books)
of different writers and different languages.
In this WOTH approach the different N N words
of a book are analogous to independent classical particles
and also analogous to households in the wealth inequality problem.
The interactions between these words (or particles)
appear due to semantic rules, meanings and writer concepts,
generating links and nonlinear couplings between them.
The precise form of these interactions is not specifically known but
this is not important when applying well known concepts of statistical physics Landau and Lifshitz (1976) ; Zakharov, L’vov, and Falkovich (1992) . For example,
as for a gas of classical particles in three dimensions
almost any weak or moderate interaction between particles
drives a system into the thermal state
with the average kinetic energy per particle 3 ​ k ​ T / 2 3kT/2 where k k and T T are
the Boltzmann constant and gas temperature.

distributed over certain states levels

The WOTH theory
gives a very good description
of the word frequencies in the 16 considered cases
but one can object that there are two fit parameters
in these RJE distributions.
However, the main competing proposal to describe work frequency
distributions based on a (shifted) power law (see e.g. Piantadosi (2014) )
also uses two or even three fit
parameters and even then it does not provide a good description at
both boundaries of the interval of the frequency distribution
(for the data used in our work). This concerns
in particular the range of small
wealth/word frequency or large rank index where the real data
curves show a strong curvature for Pareto and Zipf curves
(when shown in double logarithmic scale)
which is very well captured by the optimal RJE curves.
Concerning the Lorenz curves the agreement of data with
a shifted power law proposal is even much worse. Thus in that case the
Lorenz curve construction as such is actually very delicate and only possible
for the shifted power law proposal similar to ( 7 )
(impossible for the simple power law). On
the other hand the RJE Lorenz curves agree nearly perfectly
with the data (when shown in normal scale; modest deviations for very
small cumulated wealth values are only visible in logarithmic scale
